title: Gill and Iyer to Share ODI Captaincy as India Name Squads for New Zealand Tour
excerpt: Bumrah is picked for the Tests only, Pant awaits fitness clearance, and Kohli and Rohit feature in both ODI squads for the five-match series starting November 4 in Auckland.
body:
• Shubman Gill captains India in the first three ODIs in New Zealand and the two Tests; Shreyas Iyer takes over the ODI side for the final two matches, with Ishan Kishan as his deputy.
  • Jasprit Bumrah is picked for the Tests only and rested from the ODIs; Rishabh Pant is in the Test squad subject to fitness clearance after a left side strain.
  • Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma are in both ODI squads; wicketkeeper Kumar Kushagra earns a maiden ODI call-up, while Hardik Pandya remains absent.
  • The five ODIs run November 4–15 and the Tests start November 19 in Wellington; 7:30 a.m. IST starts mean 9 p.m. ET / 6 p.m. PT viewing the previous evening in North America.

The BCCI's selection committee has named split ODI squads and a full-strength Test squad for India's tour of New Zealand, handing Shreyas Iyer the ODI captaincy for the last two matches of the five-game series in what reads as a deliberate leadership audition before next year's ODI World Cup.

Two captains for five ODIs

According to the BCCI's announcement, Gill leads the side for the ODIs in Auckland (November 4), Wellington (November 7) and Hamilton (November 10), with Iyer as vice-captain and KL Rahul keeping wicket. For the two matches in Mount Maunganui on November 13 and 15, most of the Test-bound players leave to prepare for the red-ball leg: Iyer captains, Kishan is vice-captain and keeps wicket, and Tilak Varma, Auqib Nabi, Yash Thakur and the uncapped Kumar Kushagra come in. Kohli and Rohit stay for all five games.

Prasidh Krishna's place in the first ODI squad is marked subject to fitness clearance, and Arshdeep Singh, recently back from a shoulder injury, is named for all five matches. Bumrah is rested from the entire ODI series.

Tests: Bumrah returns, Pant waits on clearance

The Test squad, reported by Reuters, is close to full strength: Gill captains, Rahul is vice-captain, and the pace attack runs through Bumrah, Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna, Akash Deep and Anshul Kamboj. Pant, recently ruled out of the first two India A matches against New Zealand with a left side strain, is included pending medical clearance, with Dhruv Jurel as the second keeper. The spin group is Ravindra Jadeja, Washington Sundar and Kuldeep Yadav. The Tests are in Wellington from November 19 and Christchurch from November 27.

What the selections say

Three signals stand out. First, workload management is now structural: India's best fast bowler simply does not play bilateral ODIs in a Test window. Second, the Iyer captaincy stint — with a squad stripped of its senior core — is a genuine test of the next leadership tier rather than a ceremonial rotation. Third, the selectors are still widening the pool, with maiden or near-maiden picks such as Kushagra, Gurnoor Brar and Naman Dhir travelling. For diaspora fans, the tour is also conveniently timed: morning starts in New Zealand translate to prime-time evening viewing in North America.
